question.problem: Express $\frac{{x}^{2}+2x+17}{({x}^{2}+7)(x+1)}$ as a sum of partial fractions.
question.worked_solution:
Our task is to find $A,$ $B,$ and $C$ such that

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}+2x+17}{({x}^{2}+7)(x+1)} & =\frac{Ax+B}{({x}^{2}+7)}+\frac{C}{(x+1)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that since ${x}^{2}+7$ is an irreducible quadratic factor, we must use a linear term $Ax+B$ in the numerator.

We multiply both sides by $({x}^{2}+7)(x+1)$ and get

$$
{x}^{2}+2x+17=(Ax+B)(x+1)+C({x}^{2}+7).
$$

Plugging in $x=-1$ eliminates $A$ and $B$ and allows us to solve for $C.$ We get 

$$
\begin{aligned}(-1)^{2}+2(-1)+17 & =(A(-1)+B)(-1+1)+C((-1)^{2}+7) \\ 1-2+17 & =8C \\ C & =\frac{16}{8} \\ C & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Plugging in $x=0$ eliminates the $A$ term, and using our result for $C$ allows us to solve for $B.$ We get 

$$
\begin{aligned}(0)^{2}+2(0)+17 & =(A(0)+B)(0+1)+C({0}^{2}+7) \\ 17 & =B+7C \\ 17 & =B+7(2) \\ B & =17-14 \\ B & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to solve for $A,$ we choose $x=1$ and use our results for $B$ and $C.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}(1)^{2}+2(1)+17 & =(A(1)+B)(1+1)+C({1}^{2}+7) \\ 1+2+17 & =2A+2B+8C \\ 20 & =2A+2(3)+8(2) \\ 2A & =20-22 \\ A & =-\frac{2}{2} \\ A & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

So we have $A=-1,$ $B=3,$ and $C=2.$ Therefore, our final result is

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}+2x+17}{({x}^{2}+7)(x+1)}=\frac{-x+3}{({x}^{2}+7)}+\frac{2}{(x+1)}.
$$
